title: Umm al-Fatḥ bint Saʿd, the old Emperor's first child and the Emperor's half-sister, dies at fifty-one, still in the dīwān integrating the new lands
The first universities of al-Andalus open, at Ishbīliya, Qurṭuba, Gharnāṭa, Ṭulayṭula and Mālaqa

data.year: 1416 assumed (Trent's account gives 20 May after the estates panel of 31 December 1415)

title: Jadīla bint Saʿd, the heir's third wife, bears him a son, Yūsuf
Jadīla bint Saʿd leaves the work of migration and takes the dīwān's charge of the realm's peace, stabilising the country
The Emperor takes up the reform of Autocracy: the power of the state is gathered into the ruler's hands, and the men who serve him are counted members of his household

data.text: Autocratic monarchies concentrate power in the hands of the ruler. The state is often seen as their personal property. It is not uncommon for rulers to have ministers and supporters, but these are then referred to as members of the royal household (the game's text)

title: Sixteen of the twenty-one towns of the old Ṭāʾifa of Shalamanka are handed to the ṭāʾifas of the north: Shalamanka, Ciudad Rodrigo, Ledesma, Béjar, Coria and five more to Liyūn, and Ávila, Arévalo, Oropesa and three more to Burghush. Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf, freed of that work, goes to integrating the crown's lands

data.note: the far north is held through ṭāʾifas and the lands south of it integrated (Trent, January 1416)

title: Jadīla bint Yūsuf, daughter of Yūsuf I and queen of the Marīnids for thirty-five years, dies at sixty
